observation_summary: The compiler crashes with an IllegalStateException when processing a 'new' expression because it attempts to call getInstanceType() on a FunctionType that does not have an instance type.
hypothesis: The code in visitNew() assumes that if a type is a FunctionType, it must have an instance type. However, some function types (like interfaces) do not have instance types, leading to an IllegalStateException when getInstanceType() is called.
prediction: Adding a check to verify that the FunctionType has an instance type before calling getInstanceType() will prevent the crash.
experiment_rationale: The fix diff shows that the condition 'if (fnType != null)' was updated to 'if (fnType != null && fnType.hasInstanceType())'. This confirms that the root cause was a missing validation check for the existence of an instance type before accessing it.
reasoning_summary: The bug is a classic missing guard/validation check. The code was attempting to access a property (instance type) of an object (FunctionType) without verifying if that property existed, leading to an IllegalStateException. The fix adds the necessary check (hasInstanceType()) to the conditional predicate, which is the definition of a Checking defect.
evidence_used: Stack trace shows IllegalStateException at FunctionType.getInstanceType
Fix diff adds '&& fnType.hasInstanceType()' to the existing null check in TypeCheck.visitNew

alternative_types.why_not_primary: The fix is not a rewrite of the algorithm, but the addition of a guard condition to prevent an invalid state access.
